note: The one canonical action registry of ADR-K1 section 1: each action's class and target environment. Callers name an action and read these back; a caller's own label is ignored. An action not listed here is P5 (R5). Each entry names both existing vocabularies: governanceAction from core/src/permissions.ts and ownerOnlyAction from core/src/ownerOnlyActions.ts, null where that vocabulary has no spelling. Neither vocabulary is changed by this file. environment is where the executing capability acts: local when it stays on this machine, production when it reaches something live outside it, such as a third-party API or the shared remote. An action with no capability yet is production, the strictest. The boundary actions run-start, credential-release, broker-call, project-selection and bridge-read are root envelopes, never children, so R3's environment equality does not bend these values. credential-release, broker-call, commit and push are admitted only from mintCrossing, which ties them to their run.
provenance: Transcribed by the implementer (Claude) from ADR-K1 sections 3 and 4, accepted by the owner on 2026-11-01 (D3 'Accept it (Recommended)'), and from the Stage 2 delta the owner approved the same day.
trustBasis: MANUAL_GOVERNANCE_APPROVAL, tamperProof false. Read from committed bytes only and validated whole: a duplicate, a wildcard, a missing spelling or a class below its floor refuses the entire file. The floors are in core/src/actionRegistry.ts, so no edit here can lower an owner-only action (R6). Changing this file is the P5 action action-registry-change, on the same terms as tenant-registry-change, and the same limit applies: see ADR-T1 section 3.

ADR-T1 section 3: changing the tenant registry. An owner-last-commit check cannot tell the owner from an agent, so this protects nothing beyond repo write access until PROJECTOS-TENANT-PRINCIPAL1A adds an owner-only signature or an owner-gate receipt naming the registry blob sha.
ADR-T1 section 3: this file is held on the same terms as the tenant registry.

Stage 2 envelope boundary: a governed run starting. What the run then commits or spends is enveloped under its own action: its paid calls are separate P3 broker-call roots, so P2 here does not contradict ADR-K1 section 3.

Stage 2 envelope boundary: the vault releasing a secret for one operation, a root envelope tied to its run. P5. The grant for an operation release is a committed credential-release grant in the installation, naming the phase, the project, the exact references, the action and an expiry; a gatekeeper secrets-handling gate is not one, and until a grant exists operation release fails closed. Creating a grant is an owner act. Session auto-load has no owner step and is kept for a project's own project-reach credential. This prevents accidents on the kernel's routes: only provider-side scope, expiry and revocation are real boundaries until Stage 4 (ADR-T1 sections 6 and 10).

Stage 2 envelope boundary: a paid provider call through the trusted broker, a root envelope from mintCrossing, tied to its run. ADR-K1 section 3 puts paid provider calls at P3. production because it is an outbound call to a live third party, and it sends data there. A zero budget is refused.
